Regularization is introduced to tame ultraviolet (high-energy) divergences.

A. Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD)  
   • Loops are ultraviolet–divergent.  One still has to introduce a cutoff or use dimensional regularization before renormalizing, even though the coupling becomes weak at high energies (asymptotic freedom).  

B. Classical Electrodynamics  
   • The self-energy of a point charge is infinite; to make sense of it one introduces a cutoff or some other regularization.  

C. Quantum Electrodynamics (QED)  
   • Famous for its UV divergences; all loop calculations need regularization and renormalization.  

D. Superstring Theory  
   • Because fundamental objects are extended strings rather than point particles, interactions are smeared over a finite length scale.  String amplitudes are finite in the ultraviolet; no external UV regulator is required.  (Infrared issues may remain, but the question concerns high energies.)  

Hence only Superstring Theory inherently avoids the need for UV regularization.

Answer: D
